results.quote: Combining with a tournament tree, Cordon Algorithm leads to a perfect parallelization (O(L log n) work and O(k log n) span) of sequential LCS algorithm in [7]

results.previous_best: $O(n^{1.5} \log n)$ work and $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$ span (Larmore and Przytycka [69])
results.quote: Given an input sequence of size n, and the sequential GLWS algorithm Γ_lws introduced in Sec. 4.1, let k = d̂(G*_{Γ_lws}) be the effective depth of the Γ_lws-perfect DAG. Then the Cordon Algorithm for the convex GLWS has O(n log n) work and O(k log^2 n) span. It is a perfect parallelization of Γ_lws.

Given an input sequence of size n, and the sequential GLWS algorithm Γ_lws introduced in Sec. 4.1, let k = d̂(G_{Γ_lws}) be the effective depth of the Γ_lws-optimized DAG. Then the Cordon Algorithm for the concave GLWS has O(n log n) work and O(k log^2 n) span. It is an optimal parallelization of Γ_lws.

results.previous_best: $O(n^{1.5} \log^2 n)$ work and $O(\sqrt{n} \log^2 n)$ span (Larmore and Przytycka [69])
results.quote: The optimal alphabetic tree (OAT) can be constructed in O(n log^2 n) work and O(h log^3 n) span, where n is the size of input weight sequence and h is the height of the OAT.

results.problem: Optimal Alphabetic Tree (OAT) with word size W = n polylog n
results.quote: If the input key weights are positive integers with word size W=n polylog n, the OAT can be constructed in O(n log^2 n) work and polylog(n) span, where n is the input size.

The Cordon Algorithm for the GAP problem has O(mn log n) work and O(k log^2 n) span, where n and m≤n are the input size and k is the effective depth of the Γ_gap-optimized DAG for the sequential algorithm Γ_gap introduced in Sec. 5.2.
Cordon Algorithm solves Tree-GLWS in O(n log^3 n) work and O(k log^4 n) span, where k is the longest path in the best decision dependency graph.

results.bound: $O(k n \log n)$ work and $O(k \log^2 n)$ span
results.quote: Hence, the entire algorithm has O(k n log n) work and O(k log^2 n) span. In this problem, k is also the depth of the DP DAG, so this algorithm is a perfect parallelization of the classic sequential algorithm.
